comments.text:
## User-selected design direction and prototype brief — Continuum CR-01

The first collection direction is now explicit (2026-11-14):
- Hybrid design language: architectural minimalism with natural tactility and restrained technical detailing.
- Mixed fit philosophy: this robe is an adjustable wrap fit, distinct from the relaxed articulated overshirt.
- Hybrid materials: natural-fibre-led shell with localized technical materials where they measurably improve care, warmth, stability or serviceability.
- Comfort is the primary optimization objective, especially tactile comfort, seated comfort, thermal/moisture comfort, mobility and effortless don/doff.

### Product concept: “Continuum / Aperture Wrap”

A travel garment between a refined robe, wrap coat and soft over-layer. It should look intentional when worn open or closed, remain comfortable while seated for extended journeys, and transition naturally between rest, indoor wear and light outdoor movement. It is not PPE or a weatherproof coat.

**Preferred silhouette**
- Soft architectural wrap with a controlled shoulder line and generous torso ease.
- Mid-calf is the upper length boundary for concept exploration; also create a shorter knee-to-below-knee variant to compare movement, seating and packability. Avoid ankle-length excess fabric in the first sample.
- Soft sculptural shawl/fold-over collar with low-bulk neck contact.
- Raglan or kimono-derived sleeve with a separately testable underarm gusset; sleeve volume must not drag or interfere with seated use.
- Wrap overlap wide enough to retain coverage while sitting and bending; use an internal tie/loop or low-profile replaceable closure plus external belt, not belt-only closure.
- Side vents for walking and seated leg movement; vent ends reinforced without bulky skin contact.
- Two discreet angled hand pockets, positioned so their openings remain reachable while seated and do not press against the hip. One internal valuables pocket; no security/anti-theft claim.
- Adjustable sleeve turn-back or cuff tabs; avoid hard metal hardware.
- Two belt positions/loops to tune waist position; belt must be removable and replaceable.
- No electronics, battery modules or proprietary fasteners in v0.1.

### Removable warmth / lap panel

Investigate a separately removable lightweight warmth panel that attaches at discrete, concealed points inside the upper back/shoulder area and can be detached for use as a lap covering. The robe must remain complete and aesthetically resolved without it.

Design constraints:
- No exposed snaps or hard attachment points against skin.
- Attachment must not distort collar roll, shoulder balance or back drape.
- The panel must not become a loose snag hazard or interfere with belt, sleeves, seating or luggage handling.
- Compare a light quilted technical fill with a natural-fibre batting/knit alternative only if actual sourced samples exist.
- Record panel mass, packed volume, attachment cycle durability, laundering compatibility and repair process separately from shell metrics.
- Do not describe it as thermal protection; report only measured warmth/thermal resistance under the declared conditions.

### Pattern architecture — CR-01 v0.1

Patternmaker brief (not a dimensioned graded cut file):
1. Left and right front wrap panels with declared overlap extension and internal closure placement.
2. Back body with a controlled shoulder-ease option; compare clean back against a shallow inverted pleat.
3. Raglan/kimono-derived sleeve pair with grainline and sleeve pitch marked.
4. Underarm gusset as a separately versioned option.
5. Shawl/fold-over collar and front facing, with turn-of-cloth and interfacing map.
6. Pocket openings, pocket bags and reinforcement pieces.
7. Side-vent facings or bindings.
8. Belt, belt loops and internal tie/closure.
9. Internal valuables pocket.
10. Removable lap-panel shell (outer pair), optional lining, insulation layer, perimeter binding and concealed attachment tabs.
11. Soft label/loop pieces and local reinforcement.

All pieces need stable IDs, size/fit profile, cut quantity, face/orientation, grainline, notches, seam-pair IDs, edge-specific allowances, fold/roll lines, material/lot role and assembly notes. Check wrap overlap and closure retention in seated, bending and walking postures; preserve pocket access while sitting; ensure sleeve and collar do not migrate or press.

### Material strategy — local leads plus controlled alternatives

**Shell candidate A:** Millar Textiles lists a 70% cotton / 30% linen fabric at 130 gsm and also 225 gsm / 315 gsm options. Request a current 130 gsm swatch for light drape and a 225 gsm swatch only as a structured comparison. The 130 gsm cloth must be checked for opacity, crease recovery, seam slippage/fraying, body, wash stability and tactile comfort; listed specifications and current stock must be reconfirmed: https://www.millartextiles.co.za/cotton-linen/

**Shell candidate B:** a soft cotton/lyocell, cotton/viscose or fine cotton/linen woven in an approximate 120–180 gsm screening band, but only after a supplier provides an actual swatch and traceable composition. This is an unverified sourcing target, not a claim of local availability.

**Shell candidate C:** lightweight linen/ramie or cotton shirting from M&P Trikam as a locally accessible comparison. M&P lists Egyptian-cotton shirting and linen/ramie among its fashion/material ranges; obtain swatches and confirm exact weight, composition, finish and stock: https://www.mptrikam.com/ and https://www.mptrikam.com/the-finance-pulse

**Warmth panel alternatives:** compare one low-bulk quilted recycled-polyester fill and one traceable wool-based option if available. Ask for exact composition, care, fill mass/area, loft/retention, wash response and repair/recovery instructions. No supplier or recycled-content claim is accepted without evidence. A cotton/lyocell or soft woven lining can be tested for tactile interface; do not line the entire robe by default if it harms breathability, weight or packing volume.

### Prototype sequence

**CR-P0 — drape and overlap studies**
- Make three small silhouette/toile variations: (A) longer shawl-wrap, (B) shorter travel wrap, (C) hybrid with more controlled shoulder and structured pocket line.
- Use test cloths close to proposed shell weight/drape; calico alone is not an adequate drape predictor.
- Check neck comfort, overlap, seated coverage, belt migration, sleeve drag, pocket access, hem/vent behavior and don/doff.

**CR-P1 — closure and warmth-panel coupons**
- Test tie/loop, replaceable button-loop and low-profile snap options on fabric coupons.
- Test panel attachment and detachment under repeated cycles; inspect distortion, skin-side pressure and failure.
- Compare shell/panel combinations for bulk, laundering compatibility and packability.

**CR-P2 — wearable sample**
- Construct one shell sample in the chosen physical lot, with removable panel as a separate BOM and revision.
- Record as-built measurement, garment/panel mass, pack volume, balance, material IDs, sewing plan, deviations and inspection.
- Evaluate open, wrapped, belted and panel-free/panel-attached configurations.

**CR-P3 — travel-use wear evaluation**
- Test seated use for a declared duration, standing, walking, turning, stairs, reaching, bending, don/doff, bag strap interaction and access to phone/passport/wallet/water.
- Report tactile, thermal, movement, coverage, pocket-access, aesthetic and overall acceptance separately.
- Log missing data, discomfort, withdrawals and adverse interactions; participant comfort is not inferred from a sensor.

### Proposed metrics (research targets, not results)

- Zero hard coverage/closure constraints lost across the agreed task set.
- At least 90% first-attempt completion of declared don/doff and essential-pocket tasks in a formative test group, with subgroup outcomes disclosed.
- No material decline in seated comfort or movement versus the matched reference.
- Report panel attachment-cycle endurance, repair time, mass and packed volume.
- Report dimensional change/appearance after the selected ISO 6330:2021 wash/dry sequence; do not extrapolate cycles into years of service.
- Keep garment and panel qualification separate, including shell, seams, closure, pocket and panel evidence.

### Local prototype partners to approach (not yet contacted or vetted)

- African Root Studios, Sandton: advertises pattern making, grading, sampling and one-off/small-batch development; its FAQ states one-off pieces are available and standard runs begin at 20 units. Confirm whether it accepts a single robe prototype and request portfolio/quote: https://africanrootstudios.com/ and https://africanrootstudios.com/about-2/
- CG Studios, Midrand: advertises tech packs, patternmaking, fit assessment, sampling and small-batch manufacturing: https://cgstudiosjhb.co.za/
- The Joburg CMT: advertises in-house patternmaking/sampling and says its production minimum is 10 units; confirm one-off sample terms: https://www.thejoburgcmt.co.za/

No contact has been made, no quote or capacity is verified, and these are candidate vendors only.

### Claim ceiling

This design brief does not establish an approved pattern, physical prototype, all-day comfort, thermal protection, weatherproofing, security, supplier stock, manufacturing price, batch repeatability or product qualification. Exact dimensions and production pattern must follow measurement intake, material choice and physical toile review.
